strings.meta_title: StuntGP NEW — a Stunt GP reconstruction for Windows x64
strings.meta_description: StuntGP NEW is an unofficial fan reconstruction of Team17's Stunt GP for 64-bit Windows: DirectX 12, a steady 60 game steps per second and a picture that fits any aspect ratio. Download version R1.
strings.og_title: StuntGP NEW — a Stunt GP reconstruction
strings.og_description: Team17's classic radio-controlled car racer, rebuilt from the original game's code. Windows x64, DirectX 12. Version R1 available for download.
strings.brand_aria: StuntGP NEW — top of the page

strings.hero_lead: Team17's classic radio-controlled car racer — rebuilt from the original game's code and running natively on Windows x64 with DirectX 12.
strings.hero_sub: Original menus, models, textures, music and sound effects. The complete single-player game in widescreen, with frame interpolation up to your monitor's refresh rate.

strings.game_title: The original game. A new, native engine.
strings.game_p1: Stunt GP is a radio-controlled car racer on tracks full of ramps, jumps and steeply banked corners. StuntGP NEW rebuilds the whole path through the game: language selection, title screen, menus, name entry, choice of mode, vehicle and track, the race, the results and the return to the menu — all in one consistent game world.
strings.game_p2: It is neither an emulator nor a wrapper around the old EXE file. Driving mechanics, track contact, rival AI and the camera are new native code rebuilt from the instructions of the original program. The game uses the original data: models, textures, fonts, music and effects.
strings.game_p3: Where the original behaviour has not been rebuilt yet, the game reports an explicit error naming the function — instead of substituting an invented “toy” driving model.
strings.mode5_help: Race an entire Stunt GP Season.
strings.modes_note: Modes from the original game menu. Labels and help texts come straight from the game files.
strings.feat_title: Faithful to the original, comfortable on a modern PC
strings.feat1_text: Language selection, title screen, main menu, name entry, vehicle selection and track preview run on the game's original graphics, fonts and texts.
strings.feat2_text: Menu → track and mode → race → results → menu. Everything happens in one game world, with no separate preview mode.
strings.feat3_text: The simulation runs at the original pace: 60 steps per second, regardless of the monitor's refresh rate. A game step including rendering takes about 3–5 ms.
strings.feat4_text: The picture fills the window at native resolution, with no bars and no stretching. Races use Hor+ — a wider view to the sides with the original vertical field of view. The HUD sticks to the screen edges.
strings.feat5_text: Frame interpolation shows smooth motion up to your monitor's refresh rate, with pacing locked to the display. The game itself keeps 60 steps per second, so no key presses get lost and music and loading screens keep the original pace.
strings.feat6_text: Vehicle and track models, textures, fonts, music and sound effects all come from the original game files.
strings.feat7_text: Every rebuilt behaviour must point to specific instructions in the pinned original EXE file. Decompiler pseudocode alone is not accepted as proof.
strings.feat8_text: 11 documented fixes, described separately from the recovered behaviour — for example a half-second pause every 7 minutes or so, caused by a 32-bit clock counter overflowing.
strings.gal_intro: Every image is a screenshot of version R1, taken from a gameplay recording of 30 Sep 2026 — no retouching, no mock-ups. The game runs in widescreen: races, menus and results fill the whole 16:9 picture.

strings.step1_text: Download the StuntGP_NEW-R1-program.zip archive and — to be safe — compare its SHA-256 checksum.
strings.step2_text: Unpack the archive to a folder you can write to, for example the Desktop. From your own copy of Stunt GP copy the folders wads, graphics24, meshdata, sound into data\retail.
strings.step3_text: Double-click START.cmd. If a SmartScreen warning appears, choose “More info” → “Run anyway”.
strings.step4_text: On first launch, pick the menu language. On the title screen press <kbd>ENTER</kbd>, choose SINGLE PLAYER, a mode and a vehicle — and hit the track.
strings.ctl_note: The default keyboard layout comes from the original game data. <kbd>SPACE</kbd>, <kbd>SHIFT</kbd> and <kbd>CTRL</kbd> handle the original layout's extra actions.
strings.opt1: Turns frame interpolation on for this session (--no-interpolation turns it off). Normally you set it in Options → GRAPHICS → INTERPOLATE.
strings.opt2: Original 4:3 picture with bars, like ASPECT → ORIGINAL in the graphics options. The SGN_ASPECT=4x3 environment variable does the same.
strings.opt4: Environment variable: track geometry computed on the GPU. Optional, off by default.
strings.opts_note: Most settings no longer need launch options: display mode (window, borderless or exclusive fullscreen), interpolation, VSync, frame limit, anti-aliasing, texture filtering and more are in Options → GRAPHICS, and during a race under ADVANCED in the pause menu.
strings.st_title: An honest look at what's ready
strings.st_ok1: The complete single-player game: Arcade, Exhibition, Time Trial, Stunt Challenge and Championship
strings.st_ok2: Language selection, title screen, menus, name entry, vehicle and track selection
strings.st_ok3: Races against five AI rivals: start, laps, stunts and bonuses, finish, results, rankings and unlocks

strings.st_wip1: Multiplayer is not in R1 — it will be designed from scratch as a separate, networked mode
strings.st_wip2: Full visual and game-state parity with the original has not been proven yet
strings.st_wip3: The R1 build was checked with the author's visual tests and measurements; automated tests and comparisons with the original were not run for it
strings.r1_text: R1 is the first public release of StuntGP NEW. It contains:
strings.r1_item1: The complete single-player game — all five modes, from Arcade to Championship
strings.r1_item3: Widescreen: the picture fills any window, with Hor+ in races
strings.r1_item4: Frame interpolation up to the monitor's refresh rate, with display-locked pacing
strings.r1_item5: Graphics options and display modes: window, borderless and exclusive fullscreen
strings.r1_item6: The crash on exit is fixed, and the menus no longer stutter
strings.m1_text: Rebuilt behaviour must point to the pinned EXE file (SHA-256), the decompiled function and the exact instruction ranges. The decompilation is not the original source code.
strings.m2_text: Oracles run the original's unmodified instructions in the Unicorn emulator and compare the results with the new code — for example the pause and resume routines: 13,280 compared calls with no differences.
strings.m3_text: C++23, compiled with /W4 /WX — warnings treated as errors — and /fp:strict for strict floating-point arithmetic.
strings.m4_text: The window, the DirectX 12 renderer, picture scaling and presentation pacing are new code — labelled as new, not as recovered game behaviour.
strings.faq1_a: No. StuntGP NEW is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with Team17 Software Ltd. Stunt GP and Team17 are registered trademarks of Team17 Software Limited.
strings.faq2_q: Is it an emulator or a wrapper around the original EXE?
strings.faq2_a: No. It is a native x64 program written from scratch in C++23, with a DirectX 12 renderer. The original executable is not run — it serves as the reference from which the game's modules are rebuilt.
strings.faq3_a: The single-player game is complete in R1: all five modes, music and sound effects, results, rankings and unlocks. Multiplayer is not included yet — it will be designed from scratch as a separate, networked mode. Full parity with the original has not been proven yet.
strings.faq4_q: Windows shows a warning when I launch it
strings.faq4_a: StuntGP_NEW.exe is not digitally signed, so the SmartScreen filter may block it. Choose “More info” → “Run anyway”. To be safe, compare the SHA-256 checksum of the downloaded file with the value in the Download section.
strings.faq5_a: Install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable 2015–2022 (x64) from Microsoft: aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe.
strings.faq6_q: Does it work on a 144 Hz or 240 Hz monitor?
strings.faq6_a: Yes. The game runs 60 steps per second regardless of the monitor's refresh rate, and frame interpolation (Options → GRAPHICS → INTERPOLATE) shows smooth motion up to the screen's refresh rate, with pacing locked to the display.
strings.faq7_a: The picture fills the whole window with no bars, and races show a wider view to the sides (Hor+). If you prefer the original 4:3 framing, set ASPECT to ORIGINAL in the graphics options or launch the game with the --aspect-4x3 option.
strings.faq8_q: Which languages does the game menu offer?
strings.faq8_a: On first launch the game lets you choose one of the seven languages stored in the original data: English, Dutch, German, Swedish, Italian, Spanish or French. There is no Polish version of the game menu — Polish is available only on this website.
strings.faq9_q: Where does the game save its settings?
strings.faq9_a: In the save\card00 folder next to StuntGP_NEW.exe. That is why you should unpack the game somewhere you can write to — for example the Desktop, not Program Files.
strings.fin_title: Version R1 is waiting at the finish line
strings.fin_text: Download, unpack, run START.cmd — and race the original Stunt GP tracks.
